solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Banger lacking taste, but not cold

indicators.note: says the following letter is to be left out of the word before it

parts.note: something cheap is tawdry, lacking taste

explanation.surface: A sausage that has no flavour and is not served cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Banger looks like a sausage, but here it is British slang for a battered old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap and a banger are both informal names for a dilapidated old motor car.

clue.text: Reading for the faithful worthily composed

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A religious text written in a worthy manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy writ is sacred scripture, the Bible, read by believers.

clue.text: A dog biting Athenian character that's pushing it

indicators.note: the dog has the letter in its teeth, holding it inside

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A dog bites an Athenian, which is going rather far.
explanation.walkthrough: Character means a letter of an alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is a bit much means it is excessive, going too far.

clue.text: Quiet river circles wood where food may be rare

indicators.note: the quiet-and-river pair go round the wood, so the wood is placed within them

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
teak is a hardwood
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A peaceful river winding round a wood, followed by a hint at sparse provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: Rare looks like scarce, but it means lightly cooked, as a steak may be.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant specialising in steaks, which are often served rare, i.e. barely cooked.

clue.text: Tool for holding skimpy undies husband removed

indicators.note: the husband is taken out of the word

parts.note: thongs are minimal underwear

explanation.surface: Skimpy underwear, husband taken off: something to hold with.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongs are a gripping implement with two arms for picking things up.

clue.text: Relate saga's end very quietly, sure to forget chapter

indicators.note: the end of the saga is its final letter only

parts.note: the last letter of saga
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet

indicators.note: the chapter is forgotten, so it goes

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: Telling the end of a long story softly, confident enough to skip a chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: Relate looks like tell, but it is relate to, belong.
explanation.definitionFit: To appertain is to pertain or belong, to have a connection with something.

clue.text: This man is inclined to drink a port completely

indicators.note: the pair takes in the port, holding it inside

parts.note: he means this man
a ship heels when it leans to one side
Dover is an English port

explanation.surface: A man fond of a tipple, keen to down a bottle of port.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the fortified wine but is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Head over heels means entirely, as in head over heels in love.

clue.text: More invention welcomed by chateau topiarist

indicators.note: the answer is taken in by the words that follow, sitting inside them

parts.note: the six letters run across the two words, from the end of chateau into topiarist

explanation.surface: A gardener at a French chateau is pleased to receive further creativity.
explanation.walkthrough: More is Sir Thomas More, not a comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas More coined the name for his imaginary ideal society in his 1516 book.

clue.text: 10 pence secured by Ben or Holly, say, turning pro

indicators.note: the ten pence is held fast inside
the tree is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: the holly is a tree, and so is the ben, a tropical tree yielding ben oil
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Ten pence handed to Ben or Holly, who turns professional.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben and Holly look like people's names; both are trees.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is a skilled professional, a pro at their job.

clue.text: Not yet stirring filling of mint after producing pork pies

indicators.note: the middle letters come after the lying part

parts.note: pork pies is rhyming slang for lies, so producing them is lying

indicators.note: the filling is the inside, so the central letters of the word are taken

parts.note: the two central letters of mint

explanation.surface: Someone not yet up, chewing mints after telling fibs.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pies is Cockney rhyming slang: pork pies = lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in means staying in bed late, so not yet up and moving about.

clue.text: Info attendant turned up about helping divisive issue

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the attendant goes round the helping
in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
a ration is a portion, a helping

explanation.surface: Information about an attendant overturned on a matter of help.
explanation.definitionFit: The difference in attitudes between young and old is a frequent cause of family disagreement.

clue.text: Dish with a bit of the French bread dipped in ginger

indicators.note: the coin is sunk inside the word for vigour

parts.note: ginger and pep both mean energy, vigour
bread is slang for money, and a sou was a small French coin

explanation.surface: A dish served with a piece of French bread soaked in ginger.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread here is money, not a loaf; a sou was a French coin of low value.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea soup is a thick soup made from dried peas, a dish in its own right.

clue.text: Rake land in Middle East, knowing more about it

indicators.note: the word for knowing more goes round the land

parts.note: wiser means having more knowledge
Oman is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: Someone raking soil in the Middle East, getting smarter about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Rake looks like a garden tool or verb, but it is the old word for a dissolute man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a libertine, a man who habitually chases women.

clue.text: East End shopkeeper shows material for basket?

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End traditionally drop the aitch at the start of words

parts.note: a hosier sells stockings and socks

explanation.surface: A Cockney shopkeeper displays wicker for basket-making.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the Cockney part of London, where an initial H goes unsounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Osier is a willow whose pliant twigs are woven into baskets.

clue.text: Banged up vehicle parts create din, unfortunately

indicators.note: the vehicle splits the shuffled letters, sitting between them
suggests things gone wrong, so these letters come out in a different order

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A crashed car's components making an unfortunate racket.
explanation.walkthrough: Banged up looks like a damaged car, but it is British slang for put in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To be banged up is informal for being locked in a cell, i.e. imprisoned.

clue.text: Making good answer, interrupting old, irrational politician

indicators.note: the answer breaks into the others, between them

parts.note: ex means former
pi is an irrational number
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: An irrational old politician interrupted by a reply that puts things right.
explanation.walkthrough: Irrational looks like illogical, but it is the maths sense: pi is an irrational number.
explanation.definitionFit: Expiatory acts atone for wrongdoing, making amends.

clue.text: Brilliant border of alluring bedding

indicators.note: the border is its edges, the first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of alluring
litter is straw bedding for animals

explanation.surface: A dazzling trim on enticing bed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglitter means sparkling, glittering, so shining brilliantly.

clue.text: Heavenly body set off, clothed by a revolutionary designer

indicators.note: dressed by the designer, so held inside
revolving turns the designer back to front

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer

indicators.note: off means spoilt, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone set off, dressed by a radical couturier, with a gorgeous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavenly body looks like a beautiful figure, but is an object in space.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a minor planet orbiting the sun, a celestial object.

clue.text: Travelling post-haste, gent short of time may do this?

definitions.text: Travelling post-haste, gent short of time may do this?

indicators.note: the letters travel about, moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A man in a hurry, late for something, puts his foot down.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of post-haste gent minus one T rearrange to give the answer, and the whole clue describes when you would do it.
explanation.definitionFit: To step on the gas is to press the accelerator, which a driver late for an appointment would do.

clue.text: In a non-cryptic form, wanting name for cake

indicators.note: lacking the name, so it is dropped

parts.note: en clair, French for in clear, describes a message sent uncoded

explanation.surface: Plainly put, a cake lacking a name.
explanation.walkthrough: En clair is a phrase borrowed from French for a message in plain language rather than cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Teacher's aids are terrible trouble to lift up

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters are mangled
in a down clue, lifting raises the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Classroom aids are terrible trouble to carry up.
explanation.definitionFit: Realia are real objects used in teaching to illustrate daily life.

clue.text: One million lost in crime: swindle getting convictions

indicators.note: these two letters go missing from the word they are in

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to do someone is to cheat them

explanation.surface: A crime losing a million, with a fraud leading to criminal convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: Convictions looks like court verdicts, but it means firmly held beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of beliefs, a set of principles someone holds firmly.

clue.text: Endlessly working for this paper then

indicators.note: the final letter is cut off the phrase

parts.note: someone on the staff of this newspaper works at The Times

explanation.surface: A journalist toiling away for The Times without end.
explanation.definitionFit: At the time is an idiom for at that past moment, which is what then refers to.

clue.text: Go around Italy? At first, one could be here

definitions.text: At first, one could be here
definitions.note: one is a capital; this city was the first capital of unified Italy, 1861-65

indicators.note: the turn goes round the letter for Italy

parts.note: a go and a turn are both a spell in a game

explanation.surface: A tour of Italy, starting from some place.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the international vehicle code for Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The city was the original seat of government when Italy unified.

clue.text: Bagging 50, ace cricket side runs round quickly

indicators.note: the ace and side take the fifty into their bag, holding it inside

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A star batsman scores fifty and the team hurry between the wickets.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a musical direction to play briskly, at a lively pace.

clue.text: Male German teacher needs return fare from 23?

indicators.note: the combined name and title are sent back, read right to left

parts.note: Otto is a German man's name
pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A German man's teacher wants his bus fare home.
explanation.walkthrough: Fare means food, not a ticket price; 23 is TURIN, in rice-growing Piedmont.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a northern Italian rice dish, typical of Piedmont and its capital.

clue.text: Once again using program in banking

indicators.note: the program goes inside the word for banking

parts.note: banking on someone is relying on them
an app is a computer program

explanation.surface: Using software in a bank once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Reapplying is putting something into use or practice a second time.

clue.text: Start to poke with stick, perhaps?

definitions.text: Start to poke with stick, perhaps?

indicators.note: only the start of the next word is used, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of poke
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: Beginning to jab at something with a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to poke, as one might with a stick or rod.
